newsitem.title: USA: Scotsman agrees to acquire Kysor.
newsitem.headline: Scotsman agrees to acquire Kysor.

text.p: Scotsman Industries Inc said Monday it agreed to acquire Kysor Industrial Corp in a cash tender offer of $43.00 for each Kysor common and preferred share.
Scotsman manufactures commercial refrigeration products and food preparation workstations, and Kysor Industrial produces commercial refrigeration systems.
The agreement has been unanimously approved by the boards of directors of both companies, Scotsman and Kysor said in a joint statement.

The transaction, which is expected to close in the first quarter and would also include the assumption of about $30 million in Kysor debt, is expected to be non-dilutive to modestly accretive in 1997 and meaningfully accretive in 1998 to Scotsman's earnings, the company said.

In a related transaction, Kysor said it has entered into a definitive agreement for the simultaneous sale of the assets of its Transportation Products Group to Kuhlman Corp for $86 million in cash and assumption of the liabilities of the unit.

The acquisition of Kysor requires that a majority of Kysor's shares be tendered, that the sale of the Transportation Products Group to Kuhlman be closed and that the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust review period expire.
Separately, Kuhlman said it expects the acquisition of the transportation products group to add to earnings in 1997.

Scotsman, which had 1995 net sales of $324 million, makes ice machines, beverage dispensing systems, food preparation and storage equipment and related foodservice products. The company markets primarily to commercial customers in the foodservice, hospitality, beverage and health care industries.

Kysor, with 1995 sales of about $364 million, produces refrigerated display cases, commercial refrigeration systems and insulated panels for supermarkets, convenience stores and the foodservice industry.

Richard Osborne, chairman, president and chief executive officer of Scotsman, said, "By acquiring the second largest commercial refrigeration equipment provider to supermarkets (Kysor) and a significant supplier to the convenience store market, we will expand the depth and breadth of both our product lines and customer base."

George Kempton, chairman and chief executive officer of Kysor said, "In an era of consolidation in our industry, this transaction makes great strategic sense and results from our long-standing efforts to obtain maximum value for our stakeholders."
Scotsman's and Kysor's commercial products groups had combined pro forma 1996 annual revenue of about $600 million.
